start_in: If reframing: the question card, with its costed options, and the entry at status to reframe
If it starts from a candidate user flow request: its source, the flow and the step
audit_in: Need entries and flows, implemented or recetted, whose scope overlaps the need's, with their log. Selected by script, index first
audit_out: Delta: duplicate, contradiction, impact on an existing flow, option already discarded in a log, gap with the vision, principles or vocabulary (flagged, never blocking), hole
Proposed scope, drawn from the project vocabulary. To validate at the gate
Proposal: new need entry, or modification of an existing entry, with which
challenge_out: Revised need, back to the audit
The auditor's answer, read-only, quoting the entry concerned. It modifies no document: only a revised intent has an effect
write_in: In later rounds: the human's answer, or their feedback from the gate
write_out: Proposed entry (new, or modification of an existing entry), status framing: intent, non-goals, scope, and its source if the request comes from a candidate request (which then moves to "launched")
"When X, I see Y", each with its by
If the entry already exists: a new line added, with the decision, discarded alternatives and reason
Hypotheses made: each point where it chose a default value (a wording, a criterion, a scope), with the question it would have asked and its default value. It continues with that value
Only if a point blocks it: see the next step
check_in: The entry's log, before and after
check_out: Schema, cited source exists, scope from the vocabulary, when / then / by, ambiguous words, each criterion tied to a sentence of the need, each proto parcours covered
Log: previous lines unchanged, a new line if an existing entry is modified, full format (date, originating need, decision, discarded alternative, reason)
params.judge_actor: AI, four fixed questions, plus two if an existing entry is modified, citation required

judge_questions.q: Is a sentence of the need uncarried?
Is a criterion unsupported by the need sentence it cites?
Do two criteria contradict each other?
Is the reason distinct from the decision?
Is a discarded alternative really different?

judge_out: Yes or no: a sentence of the need uncarried? a criterion unsupported by the need sentence it cites? a non-observable criterion? two criteria contradicting each other?
If an existing entry is modified: is the reason distinct from the decision? is a discarded alternative really different?
gate_in: Hypotheses made by the writer, with their default value
Code checks and judge, all green
gate_out: Entry at status ready, scope, log, "new entry or modification" choice validated
Or back to the writer if wording or a hypothesis must be corrected, or to the request if the substance of the need

steps.title: Writer's question
steps.actor: Human F, only if the writer is blocked: answers its question
in: Card: the blocking point, the options, the writer's recommendation
out: Answer, back to the writer: it resumes

steps.title: Grouping
in: Other ready entries whose scope overlaps its own
Stories in forming, with their epic, whose scope overlaps the entry's
out: Proposal: join story S-n in forming, or create a new story (default choice). If the request is broad: place it in an epic, existing or to create, otherwise no epic
Short explanation: why these entries go together, in three sentences at most

steps.title: Code checks
out: Cited story exists and is in forming, cited epic exists, each entry in exactly one story, an explanation present

steps.title: Gate · Grouping
out: Grouping validated: story, and epic if any
Or correction: another story, a split, an epic. Back to the grouping AI with this correction

steps.title: Need ready
out: Entry ready, criteria and scope validated

Story: created for this entry, or entry added to a story in forming. A single-entry story is ready to design right away. A multi-entry story stays "forming" until human F closes it. Epic: created or joined if the request is broad. Statuses are derived by script, except closing

contract: A raw request (with an accepted proto if any), an entry to reframe sent back by Plan, Build or the Recette, a candidate request from a user flow, a report qualified "uncovered behavior", or the catch-up of a provisional express criterion.
A need entry at status ready, with validated criteria and scope, attached to a story, itself possibly in an epic, after two validations: the criteria, then the grouping.
Human F, at two gates: the criteria, then the grouping. No human T.
notes: When the challenge opens

A script opens it only if the auditor's delta is not empty. Otherwise writing follows directly. The discussion is a loop between the human and the auditor, with no maximum number of rounds: at each round, the auditor receives the delta and the messages exchanged since its last round.
Decision log

Section of the entry, append-only: each modification of an existing entry adds a line with the decision, discarded alternatives and reason. The auditor reads it to spot a request that revives an already-discarded option. Adopted for now, to revise with use.
What blocks the writer

A point is blocking when a choice is covered by no decision or guideline, and its options differ in effect or cost. The writer then asks a question, with the options and its recommendation. Everything else becomes a hypothesis made, visible at the gate.
The writer proceeds, the human decides at the gate

Without a block, the writer continues and the checks chain. The human is asked before the gate only if a point blocks the writer. At the gate, they can send everything back to the writer. No maximum number of rounds.
New entry or modification

A need that touches an already-described feature modifies its entry, with a log line. Otherwise it creates one. The auditor proposes it in its delta and the human confirms at the gate. A feature is never removed: it evolves, through a regular need.
Closing a story or an epic

While a multi-entry story is forming, it accepts more entries. Human F closes it by an explicit action, and it becomes "ready to design". A single-entry story is so by default. An epic closes the same way, once its stories are formed.
Epic, story, task: GitHub issues

A story is a thin issue pointing to its wiki entries, without copying their text. It groups one or more entries that make sense together and are built together. An epic is the parent issue of several stories. Tasks, sub-issues of a story, come from Plan.
Two gates, two questions

The first validates the substance: what the feature must do, with its criteria. The second validates the grouping, on already-validated entries, with a short explanation. A grouping can be corrected while the story is forming: so there is no validator or judge, only code checks.
Functional split here, technical elsewhere
Need groups entries into stories and stories into an epic, by functional meaning. Splitting a story into tasks depends on the code: that is the role of Plan.
Criteria are the tests
Human F validates observable sentences. The Build workflow turns them into tests that fail before any code.
doc.lede: A request becomes a wiki entry with observable criteria, validated by human F. These criteria will become the tests.
